speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I see you're feeling agitated and have noticed some yellowing of your skin and eyes. When did you first start noticing these symptoms, and have you experienced any abdominal pain or changes in your urine color?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any abdominal pain, fever, or dark urine, and have you noticed any recent weight loss or fatigue? I also need to know if you have a history of Hepatitis B vaccination or any other liver conditions.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify if you have dark urine or abdominal pain, as these are key signs of liver stress. Additionally, given your high-risk sexual history and drug use, I need to rule out acute viral hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin: 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST: 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT: 650 IU/L (elevated), TP_Activity: < 40% (reduced), INR: 1.5 (elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text: Those results indicate severe liver injury, so I need to pinpoint the cause. Have you experienced any nausea, vomiting, or loss of appetite, and have you had any recent unprotected sexual encounters or shared needles? REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_A_IgM, Hepatitis_B_Surface_Antigen, Hepatitis_C_Antibody

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the viral hepatitis panel is negative, I need to rule out other causes of acute liver failure such as acetaminophen toxicity or autoimmune hepatitis. Have you taken any acetaminophen (Tylenol) or herbal supplements recently, and do you have any joint pain or skin rashes? REQUEST TEST: Acetaminophen_Level, Autoimmune_Hepatitis_Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of cocaine and ecstasy use, I need to rule out rhabdomyolysis or toxic hepatitis from these substances. REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Kinase, Urine_Tox_Screen

speaker: Doctor
text: With viral hepatitis, acetaminophen toxicity, and rhabdomyolysis ruled out, I suspect an autoimmune etiology or Wilson's disease given your age and presentation. REQUEST TEST: Anti-Smooth_Muscle_Antibody, Serum_Copper, Ceruloplasmin

speaker: Doctor
text: With autoimmune markers and Wilson's disease ruled out, I must consider other metabolic causes like acute fatty liver of pregnancy or Reye's syndrome, though the latter is less likely in an adult. Have you experienced any recent severe influenza or chickenpox infections, or taken aspirin recently? REQUEST TEST: Blood_Glucose, Ammonia_Level

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated ammonia confirms hepatic encephalopathy, but with common causes ruled out, I need to consider acute liver failure secondary to a rare infection or toxin. Have you consumed any energy drinks, herbal supplements, or mushroom-based products recently, or experienced any recent tick bites? REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_E_IgM, Leptospira_Antibody

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the patient's age, high-risk sexual behavior, and negative workup for common viral and toxic causes, this presentation is highly suggestive of acute primary Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) infection causing fulminant hepatitis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute EBV Hepatitis
